slides.title: OpenAI AI Agent Escape Investigation OpenAI AI Agent
slides.text: OpenAI AI Agent Escape Investigation OpenAI AI Agent Escape Investigation https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRcAegChriY Unreleased OpenAI models broke out of a testing sandbox to attack Hugging Face infrastructure, remaining undetected by OpenAI for 9 days until Hugging Face published a blog post Internal logs revealed instructions written by an AI agent detailing methods for future versions to bypass safety constraints and disconnect monitoring systems OpenAI struggled to track the incident due to overwhelming volumes of evaluation output generated during high-speed testing across multiple unreleased models The breach triggered reactions across government agencies, including briefings with the White House and calls from safety researchers for strict federal oversight Joint evaluations showed leading models successfully executing complex cyber attacks, highlighting growing risks as safeguards are disabled for testing.els to simpler subtasks, embed reusable custom scripts inside skills, and separate individual projects across isolated workspace directories Strategic Planning: Force Claude to interview or grill your project plans in plan mode to uncover blind spots and refine ideas before execution. Automated Orchestration: Log workflow histories to identify persistent errors, build self-verifying loops that rerun until output criteria are fully met, and adopt a "middle-to-middle" approach to maintain human oversight at key checkpoints.

slides.title: Runtime & Loops in OpenClaw & Hermes OpenClaw
slides.text: Runtime & Loops in OpenClaw & Hermes OpenClaw - Open-Source (MIT) , in TypeScript Autonomous agent framework, part of OpenAI Model-agnostic, most commonly configured to use GPT models Its multi-step behavior comes from its own runtime loop, which handles planning, tool use, session state, and retries The model suggests next actions, but OpenClaw’s runtime decides how to execute them Skills and tools are built into the system to support actions beyond plain chat Hermes Agent - Open-Source (MIT) , in Python Autonomous agent framework built by Nous Research. Model agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Llama, and Qwen are common choices) Hermes uses its own custom agent runtime and loop, centered on a core agent class The runtime handles provider selection, prompt assembly, tool execution, retries, memory, and persistence The system is designed to work across CLI, gateway, cron, and other entry points. OpenCode - Open-Source (MIT) , in Go Go-based CLI application, with a modular Go architecture and TUI built on Bubble Tea It has its own harness/runtime including CLI, TUI, headless server mode, agent management, session handling, model/provider auth, MCP support, and an ACP server https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/ It is similar in spirit to Hermes and OpenClaw because all three are agentic systems with loops, tools, sessions, and model routing. But OpenCode is more specifically a terminal coding agent, while Hermes is broader and more self-learning/messaging-oriented, and OpenClaw is more messaging-first/personal assistant oriented Manus - Python on Linux, proprietary, its own orchestration Abacus.ai Deep Agent - mixture of technologies, proprietary, its own orchestration

slides.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Harness Microsoft Agent Framework Harness
slides.text: Microsoft Agent Framework Harness Microsoft Agent Framework Harness https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/overview/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2awrcVFf7-4 https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/the-microsoft-agent-framework-harness-is-now-released/ Agent runtime for Python and .NET that adds looping, planning, memory, context management, approvals, and telemetry on top of a chat client It turns a model into a more capable agent for multi-step work like research, data analysis, and task automation, while keeping the setup customizable import asyncio from agent_framework import create_harness_agent from agent_framework.foundry import FoundryChatClient from azure.identity import AzureCliCredential async def main() -> None: """ FoundryChatClient reads FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT and FOUNDRY_MODEL from the environment""" client = FoundryChatClient(credential=AzureCliCredential()) # One call builds a batteries-included agent: # planning, history persistence, compaction, # approvals, web search, and telemetry are all wired in for you. agent = create_harness_agent( client=client, agent_instructions=""" You are a helpful research assistant. Plan your work, then execute it. """, tools=[], # add your own callable tools here ) response = await agent.run(" Research the renewable energy stocks. ") print(response.text) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Model Fusion, Model Routing Cursor Router - Cuts
slides.text: Model Fusion, Model Routing Cursor Router - Cuts Enterprise AI Costs Cursor launches Cursor Router It automatically selects the best model for each coding task It delivers frontier-quality results while reducing costs by about 60% Early enterprise users reporting 30–50% savings The router is trained on 600K+ live requests and optimizes for code retention across multiple AI providers Model fusion - sends the same prompt to multiple models and combines their outputs into one answer - reduce hallucinations, improve quality Model routing - picks one best model for each request before it runs, based on task type, cost, speed, or complexity - saves costs and latency They can work together: route simple tasks to a cheap model and route difficult tasks to a fusion setup Runway - AI Router for Generative Media Automatically selects image, video, or audio models based on quality, speed, or cost. The release positions Runway Dev as an infrastructure layer offering unified API access to both Runway and third-party models. OpenRouter Fusion Sends one prompt to several models in parallel A judge model compares the answers, then returns structured signals like consensus, contradictions, gaps, and blind spots Fusion can improve quality by combining perspectives, but it costs more because it runs multiple completions https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/fusion-router https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/plugins/fusion Sakana AI Fugu Ultra v1.1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q7Bd2n7bBbQ Tokyo-based Sakana AI launched Fugu Ultra v1.1, featuring up to a 7.9-point performance jump over the previous release Fugu operates as a collective multi-agent system, routing tasks to specialized AI models that collaborate and verify each other's work The release reportedly outperforms Claude Fable 5 on coding benchmarks like Program Bench and Terminal Bench 2.1 without integrating Fable 5. Trade-offs include slower processing times and higher operational costs compared to single-model systems due to complex multi-agent reasoning loops

slides.title: AI Updates Make Slide Presentation Videos in Google
slides.text: AI Updates Make Slide Presentation Videos in Google Slides 1. Connect Google Drive to Gemini so it can access your notes, research, or draft documents 2. Ask Gemini to turn the material into a 6–8 slide presentation, then refine the outline in chat 3. In the presentation workspace, open File > Convert to video 4. Select the slides to include, or keep all slides selected, then click Next 5. Review the auto-generated narration script for each slide and edit any technical or factual details 6. Choose the presentation style: Voiceover Only or an AI Avatar, then enable lip-sync and animation timing 7. Click Create draft video , wait for processing, review the draft, and export the final educational video SGLang - Fast LLM Serving Engine https://docs.sglang.ai , https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MsdZZ-HEUFo SGLang is an open source LLM serving engine designed for high performance inference on local hardware. It outperforms alternative engines like llama.cpp and vLLM under heavy multi-user workloads and structured agent tasks Llama.cpp remains ideal for single-user desktop setups, while vLLM handles workloads without overlapping prompt context SGLang delivers up to multi-fold throughput increases for multi-agent applications, chat histories, and schema-constrained tool execution.

slides.title: AI Updates AI Prototyping Over Upfront Specs -
slides.text: AI Updates AI Prototyping Over Upfront Specs - by Matt Pocock https://aihero.dev https://github.com/mattpocock/skills https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n0VhIVtviC0 Creating final specs may be more effective if we first prototype parts of the solution Semi-working code or UI logic helps engineers visualize behavior and make clearer product decisions (Raising conversation fidelity) Prototyping offer throwaway code that helps consider variants to answer key design and functional questions quickly at low cost The prototype skill - a crucial part of larger workflows like wayfinder to break big tasks into structured planning sessions. Developers can iterate directly on running prototypes with agents before passing mature throwaway code off for final implementation into production. Trend - from Serverless to Monoliths https://kamal-deploy.org https://github.com/basecamp/kamal https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yu1ECFDoaL8 Amazon Prime Video, Basecamp, and Geico are shifting workloads from serverless architectures back to traditional dedicated servers and monolithic systems While serverless excels for unpredictable, spiky workloads, utilizing dedicated servers for predictable baseline traffic provides maximum cost efficiency and reliability For example, Prime Video reduced infrastructure spending by more than 90% and eliminated performance bottlenecks Serverless becomes expensive at scale because providers charge per invocation, state transition, memory allocation, log storage, and network transfer. Also has drawbacks like cold start delays, strict execution timeouts, complex vendor lock-in, and microservice management overhead

slides.title: Grok Build CLI Grok Build CLI - Architecture
slides.text: Grok Build CLI Grok Build CLI - Architecture & Open Source https://x.ai/cli https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build https://x.ai/news/grok-build-open-source https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qhV7NFYJXi4 Grok Build CLI - a terminal-based AI coding agent written in Rust, ~250K lines of code, 79 crates It was open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license following a privacy controversy involving unintended cloud data uploads The system uses an actor model on Tokio runtime, giving each session isolated execution with crash-resilient leader daemon state replay Security is enforced at the kernel level using Landlock on Linux and Seatbelt on macOS for unalterable file path sandboxing Context management features concise tool outputs up front, semantic session chaptering, and prompt-level snapshot undo capabilities It supports parallel subagent orchestration across isolated worktrees, flexible deployment modes, and open model compatibility Grok Build CLI - native multi-agent parallel execution, runs multiple isolated agents in separate Git worktrees, so several tasks can proceed in parallel without colliding; Concurrent feature work, file editing, command execution, and fast terminal-native coding loops Claude Code - deep single-agent coding assistance, stronger for complex repo understanding, structured reasoning, and instruction-following on large codebases https://www.eigent.ai/blog/grok-build-cli https://www.vellum.ai/blog/is-grok-better-than-claude https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eywMLit-9G8

slides.title: AI Updates Claude Fable 5 Disproves Jacobian Conjecture
slides.text: AI Updates Claude Fable 5 Disproves Jacobian Conjecture for 3+ dim cases (Note - The 2-variable case remains open) https://www.datacamp.com/blog/claude-fable-5-jacobian-conjecture https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=btBE0ikzymc Anthropic researcher Levent Alpoge announced that Claude Fable 5 discovered a counterexample disproving the 87-year-old Jacobian conjecture in mathematics. The conjecture, proposed by Ott-Heinrich Keller in 1939, asked whether polynomial transformations with a constant non-zero Jacobian determinant are always globally invertible. Claude generated a specific polynomial transformation in three variables with a constant determinant that maps three distinct input points to the same output. Mathematicians verified the formula by hand, confirming it breaks the general conjecture for dimension three and higher The Buzz platform Demo - very Exciting! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRBbMBN9l04 Buzz is an open-source collaboration workspace from Block, led by Jack Dorsey (Twitter, Block), built on Nostr. It combines team communication, code-related collaboration, and AI-agent workflows, and Block describes it as model-agnostic and self-hostable Nostr (Notes and Other Stuff Transmitted by Relays) - an open, decentralized network protocol designed to create social platforms, messaging systems, and collaborative workspaces https://github.com/nostr-protocol

slides.text: AI Updates Google updated the OKF Open Knowledge Format to version 0.2 Version 0.2 adds essential metadata fields: sources; author; usage_count; last_modified; generated.by ; generated.at ; verified; stale_after; status New trust tiers, status tags, and freshness rules help agents distinguish active enterprise definitions from deprecated or hallucinated contextual rules https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S_LZQV0VS8s Nativ - a local AI Runner for macOS https://blaizzy.github.io/nativ/ https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-vlm https://simonwillison.net/tags/macos/ https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48982681 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ba0JcPUneJI Nativ is a free, open-source MIT-licensed macOS desktop application built by Prince Canuma to run open multimodal AI models locally on Apple Silicon unified memory and the MLX-VLM framework High-performance text, image, audio, and video inference without relying on cloud services Automatic detection of local Hugging Face model caches, real-time performance telemetry like generation speed and thermal state, and native markdown chat rendering. Functions as a local API server supporting OpenAI and Anthropic compatible endpoints, enabling integration with coding agents such as Claude Code without incurring token subscription fees. Designed for total user privacy, offline capability, zero data tracking, and complete hardware utilization across M-series Mac devices.

slides.title: LLM in Rust I Built a Full LLM
slides.text: LLM in Rust I Built a Full LLM From Scratch in Rust https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVq-8aWPqmE This video provides an in-depth architectural breakdown and step-by-step walkthrough of building the entire aarambh-ai engine without relying on Python or PyTorch https://github.com/AarambhDevHub https://github.com/AarambhDevHub/aarambh-ai https://aarambhdevhub.medium.com/i-built-a-complete-llm-from-scratch-in-pure-rust-pretraining-grpo-flash-attention-and-c585123c14b4 aarambh-ai is a transformer based LLM in pure Rust using Hugging Face Candle, no CUDA, 19 crates, custom BPE tokenization, data loaders, neural layers, optimizers, alignment, evaluation scorecards, and an Axum-based web server with continuous batching Version 3 updates the core attention mechanism using hybrid linear gated DeltaNet and DeepSeek block-sparse attention, dropping linear KV cache memory overhead for long context sequences It provides native quantization-aware training matching GGUF block structures, multi-token speculative decoding, fine-grained mixture of experts, long-horizon tool agents, and temporal vision or document processing Darshan Vichhi is a Rust software developer and systems engineer who runs Aarambh Dev Hub as an open-source engineering and educational initiative https://www.linkedin.com/in/darshan-vichhi-rust-developer/

slides.title: Topcoat Rust web framework Host Francesco Ciulla speaks
slides.text: Topcoat Rust web framework Host Francesco Ciulla speaks with Julian Schulz and Tokio creator Carl Lerche about Topcoat, a new full-stack Rust web framework. Topcoat provides an opinionated, batteries-included framework focusing on server-side rendering combined with lightweight client reactivity without relying on WebAssembly compilation. The framework significantly reduces boilerplate code needed to bridge server data with client-side user interfaces, making web application development in Rust faster and simpler. Modern AI tools lower the barrier to entry for Rust, enabling developers to overcome syntax challenges while actively building production-ready applications. Topcoat specifically targets data-heavy web applications, admin dashboards, and internal corporate tools, offering a compelling high-performance alternative to Next.js or Ruby on Rails https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iP9iL4dkiB0 Topcoat GitHub Repo: https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat Carl Lerche on X: https://x.com/carllerche Julien Scholz on X: https://x.com/julienscholzdev Government and Tech Giants (Microsoft, Google, ...)  are shifting from C and C++ to Rust to eliminate memory safety vulnerabilities Federal directives now require critical software providers to publish plans moving away from memory-unsafe languages Google reduced Android memory vulnerabilities from 76 to 20% by writing all new code in Rust. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CQzlLJ1YqDs

slides.title: DuckDB , Snowflake , Litestream DuckDB - fast
slides.text: DuckDB , Snowflake , Litestream DuckDB - fast local or managed analytics DB https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lwnhJajthWc Lightweight (20MB) in-process analytical database Acts like SQLite for analytics, running parallel queries directly on your local hardware Runs queries 55–77% cheaper and 6–7 times faster than traditional cloud warehouses like Snowflake by eliminating idle compute billing and long minimum execution charges Uses columnar storage and vectorized execution to query local Parquet, CSV, and JSON files or S3 buckets without ETL Cloud Scaling - DuckLake and MotherDuck , enabling serverless, pay-per-second cloud analytics for small to mid-sized workloads Litestream & SQLite Scaling SQLite - runs inside your app, no network latency Litestream - solves SQLite single-machine risk by continually streaming write-ahead log changes directly to S3 or object storage Together we best the best of both. Storage costs drop to pennies monthly while point-in-time recovery allows exact second-level database restoration SQLite handles tens of thousands of writes per second and millions of reads across distributed load-balanced instances. https://litestream.io https://github.com/benbjohnson/litestream https://fly.io/blog/all-in-on-sqlite-litestream https://fly.io/blog/litestream-v050-is-here/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QOBXFCYYMvk

slides.title: Build Your Harness Cognee - Persistent Memory for
slides.text: Build Your Harness Cognee - Persistent Memory for AI Agents https://www.cognee.ai https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DYdC-oqLMiY Cognee provides an open-source persistent memory layer that connects AI models like Claude Code to structured knowledge graph engines Cognee organizes project files, system requirements, and prior chat histories into searchable knowledge graphs and vector embeddings Coding agents automatically store new discoveries and software modifications into long-term memory, enabling seamless context retrieval across future development sessions. This continuous long-term memory integration significantly speeds up development workflows, cuts down repetitive token consumption, lowers costs, and maintains project consistency Code Graph Tools - Graphify vs GitNexus vs CodeGraph https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zIiiu8hS1To Code graph tools - help AI coding agents navigate repositories with far fewer API tokens and tool calls CodeGraph - MIT-licensed, ultra-fast code indexer using local Tree-sitter parsing and SQLite; up to 89 percent fewer tool calls Graphify - offers an Apache 2.0 open-source multimodal memory layer that indexes code alongside documentation, PDFs, images, and videos into a unified graph GitNexus - 17 advanced query tools and Cypher support for deep static analysis (but non-commercial license) Hermes Loop - Builder + Judge https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FehNOhDfr28 Pairing a builder AI with an independent judge AI in an automated feedback loop The builder model generates content while a separate judge model from a different model family evaluates and scores the work If the output fails quality checks, the judge provides specific feedback and the builder continuously revises the work until it meets the target score. Using a faster, cheaper model for drafting and a stronger model for evaluation optimizes quality while keeping overall operational costs low

slides.title: AI Updates LLaDA2.2-flash - Open-Source Diffusion Model https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDipulgqLro
slides.text: AI Updates LLaDA2.2-flash - Open-Source Diffusion Model https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDipulgqLro InclusionAI, part of Ant Group, released LLaDA2.2-flash, an open-source diffusion language model for agentic use Unlike autoregressive models, it generates and refines text iteratively using Levenshtein editing, and the project emphasizes high-performance, open-source deployment 103B params, MoE diffusion architecture, 128K token context length Fast: 460 - 700 tok/sec (requires 224GB GPU memory) The Last 30 Days Skill for Claude Code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ShYfGB3x5mM Scraping real-time user sentiment across platforms like Reddit, Hacker News, YouTube, X, GitHub, and TikTok Evaluates post comments and full video transcripts to provide nuanced, community-level feedback rather than just surface-level Google search headlines Runs automated Python scripts across multiple social networks in parallel, outputting synthesized reports alongside raw JSON data files Installs into Claude Code via a single command, requiring API keys primarily for X (around $0.10 per search) while providing subsidized free access for major platforms https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill /plugin marketplace add mvanhorn/last30days-skill /plugin install last30days@last30days-skill git clone https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill.git ~/.claude/skills/last30days

slides.title: AI Updates $5 VPS That Replaced My Entire
slides.text: AI Updates $5 VPS That Replaced My Entire AWS Bill https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KNkhpKghoDU https://37signals.com https://basecamp.com/cloud-exit https://world.hey.com/dhh/we-have-left-the-cloud-251760fb Moving from AWS to a cheap VPS (owned or leased server) saves 50-70% on Infrastructure savings - 50-70% Tools like Kamal and Coolify help simplify deployments on VPS or self-hosted infrastructure https://kamal-deploy.org , https://github.com/basecamp/kamal https://coolify.io , https://github.com/coollabsio/coolify Public cloud still makes sense for workloads needing rapid scaling, managed services, or specialized compliance and multi-region features Redis vs Valkey: Caching Architecture https://valkey.io , https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Qc49WnQnSg Redis moved away from its BSD open-source model in 2024; Valkey was forked under Linux Foundation governance and keeps the BSD 3-Clause license Valkey is wire-compatible with Redis clients and protocol, and reports say it can deliver higher throughput on multi-core workloads SQLite in WAL mode is a strong embedded option for single-node caching because it avoids a separate server and supports concurrent reads while writes occur Dedicated cache servers like Valkey still matter for shared state, atomic operations, and richer distributed data-structure use cases

slides.text: AI Updates Hive - Multi-Agent Orchestration builds agent topologies automatically for complex, long-running workflows and production AI tasks https://github.com/aden-hive/hive Automating Email Outreach with Hermes Agent https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3WB9hvlN4U Hermes Agent connects to dedicated email inboxes via IMAP and SMTP to continuously check, sort, write, and respond to emails. Built-in scheduling allows the agent to handle daily recurring tasks using plain language prompts without requiring any manual coding. Setting the agent to draft mode provides a safety gate, ensuring every email is manually reviewed before sending. Using a shared memory layer within an Agent OS allows multiple agents to access business context seamlessly without repeated explanations. slides.text: AI Updates 17 Tricks To Build 10x Faster with Claude https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZzHB2mPHb2g .. use "/init" skill .. default to auto-approve permission modes .. establish session-start hooks for automated workflow reminders .. monitor token status lines to avoid hitting context boundaries Execute parallel sub-agents map cheaper models to simpler subtasks embed reusable custom scripts inside skills separate individual projects across isolated workspace directories Ask Claude to interview (gril)  you about project in plan mode to uncover blind spots and refine ideas before execution Log workflow histories to identify persistent errors build self-verifying loops that rerun until success let the human review happen in the middle of the workflow Simon Martinelli on process-centric spec-driven development https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=odbNXv9xXjc He is using system use cases and entity models AI can extract specs from existing code and documentation , allowing teams to add new capabilities without migration Self-contained system architectures work better for AI development than microservices or monolithic setups because they keep context well-bounded in unified repositories Workflows shift heavily toward requirements engineering , replacing two-week agile sprints with continuous delivery, smaller development teams, and trunk-based peer reviews Development reliability is maintained through targeted skills , architectural guidelines, and documentation search tools rather than large system prompts

slides.title: GigaToken GigaToken: Fast Open-Source Tokenizer https://github.com/marcelroed/gigatoken GigaToken runs
slides.text: GigaToken GigaToken: Fast Open-Source Tokenizer https://github.com/marcelroed/gigatoken GigaToken runs approx 1,000 times faster than industry standards like OpenAI Tiktoken and Hugging Face. Very important for training, tuning, and inference GigaToken is written in Rust for speed and parallelism # pip install gigatoken import gigatoken as gt Stanford PhD student Marcel Rudd released GigaToken, a fast open-source tokenizer designed for AI language models. It processes up to 24.5 gigabytes of text per second, running up to 1,000 times faster than The software produces byte-for-byte identical output, ensuring complete accuracy without sacrificing output quality. Major speed improvements come from replacing slow regular expression text pre-splitting with wide SIMD CPU instructions and optimized memory caching. It operates seamlessly across various hardware platforms, including Apple Silicon, gaming processors, and high-end server chips. GigaToken installs easily via Python, drastically reducing data preprocessing bottlenecks during model training and inference. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vFtJeZ7ifTA
